text: This is the core of the proof: FTC Part 2 (integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt) turns the integration problem into a differentiation problem. Since we already proved dA/dr = C(r) in the companion entry, the FTC hands us the result directly.
Continuity implies integrability: any continuous function is Riemann integrable on any bounded interval. Mathlib's `Continuous.intervalIntegrable` packages this fact for us.
After applying FTC, the goal becomes circleArea r - circleArea 0 = circleArea r. The `simp [circleArea]` closes this by computing circleArea 0 = π * 0² = 0.
The annulus area formula generalizes the disk area: the area between two circles of radii r₁ and r₂ is π(r₂² - r₁²). This follows from the same FTC argument applied on [r₁, r₂] instead of [0, r].

This theorem closes the circle (FTC duality): differentiating the integral ∫₀ˢ C(ρ) dρ recovers C(s). Combined with the main theorem, we have A = ∫C and C = A' — the full FTC package for circle geometry.
